submitter: site_delivery_and_editor lane, bugs_open/474 — found on the first run of delivery-review-filer ever, during the owner-authorised delivery rehearsal.
rationale:
The owner cannot approve a delivery review. He opens the item, the "Approve & Continue" button is there, he presses it, and gets "No review data to approve" — nothing recorded, no error naming what is missing, delivery gate shut. Found BEFORE he clicked, because the rehearsal was run on a non-customer site first; on a paying customer this would have been discovered by the customer waiting.

THE MISMATCH. The admin screen derives everything it submits from `spec.review_data` (App.tsx:519 sets editedReviewData only if `spec.checkpoint && spec.review_data`; :762 handleApprove returns early without it). But the BUTTON's visibility condition is `isCheckpoint` alone (:1295) — so it renders for an item it cannot submit, which is what turns a shape mismatch into a dead end rather than an absence. HandleApproveWorkItem would refuse it a layer further back too (ReviewData is binding:"required").

WHY ONLY THIS PRODUCER. Every other checkpoint item is filed by `checkpoint_for_review`, which always writes review_data. `delivery-review-filer` is the one that files a checkpoint through `create_work_item`, which does not. [MEASURED 2026-09-03, all history] across every row with `spec->>'checkpoint'='true'`: 26 carry review_data, exactly ONE does not, and it is the only delivery review ever filed. A second producer with the same gap would have shown in that census.

OUR OWN CODE PREDICTED THIS AND DISMISSED IT. platform/delivery/prepare.go's ReviewItemRequiredSpec carries the parenthesis: "(The approve endpoint additionally requires a non-empty review_data JSON body from the CALLER of the API — the admin screen's concern, not the producer's, so it is noted here and not encoded.)" The observation is right and the conclusion is wrong: the screen has no source for review_data other than the item's own spec, so caller and producer are the same concern. That parenthesis is why the requirement was written down and still not met.

SCOPE: one key on one agent's step config. No Go, no roll, live on apply. The frontend half (make the button's visibility match its action) is candidate 2 in the bug file and is deliberately NOT in this change.

plan.summary: Point delivery-review-filer's `spec_paths.review_data` at `input_data` — the map it was already given, holding exactly the site_id, domain, site_url and brief the owner is being asked to review. One key, no dispatcher has to remember anything, no placeholder value.

edits.rationale: Chosen after READING create_work_item's resolver rather than guessing at it (create_work_item_action.go:266-305): `spec_data` copies a map's entries in FLAT, `spec_paths` assigns `specMap[key] = val` also FLAT, `spec_literal` is verbatim constants. None of the three can ASSEMBLE a nested object from separate input fields — but spec_paths can POINT a key at a map that already exists, because ExtractNestedField returns whatever is at the path, map included. Rejected alternative: `spec_paths: {review_data: input_data.review_data}` with every dispatcher composing the object. It has one real merit — an unresolved spec_path is a HARD ERROR, so a forgetful dispatcher would fail loudly at file time rather than silently produce an unapprovable item — but it moves work onto every future caller to fix a defect none of them caused.
edits.sketch:
jsonb_set(default_config,'{workflow,steps,file_review,config,spec_paths}',
  (…->'spec_paths') || jsonb_build_object('review_data','input_data'), false)
-- plus a one-row patch of the already-filed item, built from ITS OWN spec:
-- spec || jsonb_build_object('review_data', jsonb_build_object(
--   'domain',spec->>'domain','site_url',spec->>'site_url','brief',spec->>'brief'))

grounded_in: App.tsx:519-520 — editedReviewData set only if spec.checkpoint && spec.review_data.
App.tsx:762-766 — handleApprove: `if (!editedReviewData) { setMessage("No review data to approve"); return; }` — it posts nothing.
App.tsx:1295 — the Approve button renders on `isCheckpoint && status === 'needs_human_review'`, which does NOT include the condition that makes it work.

[MEASURED 2026-09-03, all history] rows with spec->>'checkpoint'='true' grouped by `spec ? 'review_data'`: copy_edit_proposed 21 with, needs_human_review 7 with, needs_delivery_review 1 WITHOUT. One gap in the estate, and it is the only delivery review ever filed.
checkpoint_for_review_action.go:157 — the other producer always writes review_data, which is why no other item type has this gap.
create_work_item_action.go:266-305 — the three spec layers, all flat; spec_paths resolves each value individually via ExtractNestedField, so it can point at a map but cannot build one.
platform/delivery/prepare.go, ReviewItemRequiredSpec — the parenthesis naming this requirement and assigning it to someone else.
